newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigeria licences 20 indigenous oil firms - paper.
newsitem.headline: Nigeria licences 20 indigenous oil firms - paper.

text.p: Nigeria's military government gave operating licences to about 20 indigenous oil firms in 1996, the official Daily Times newspaper said on Friday.

There was no immediate comment from the oil ministry but the newspaper said the firms were granted oil prospecting licences (OPLs) to promote local participation in the upstream sector of Nigeria's oil industry, the nation's economic lifeline.
The beneficiaries include Amni Petroleum, Dubri Oil, Yinka Folawiyo, Brass Petroleum and Nigerian Petroleum Development Company, the exploration arm of state oil giant NNPC.
Some of the firms are already operating in partnership with foreign oil companies and have announced some oil finds.
Daily Times, which is majority owned by the government, said the military authorities were likely to approve tax concessions for the local oil firms in this year's fiscal budget.

Their trade group, the National Association of Indigenous Petroleum Explorers, has already advocated pioneer status for its members which entails granting them tax exemption for five years and payment of royalties after 10 years of operation.

The military government hopes these incentives will help raise Nigeria's oil output capacity to four million barrels per day (bpd) and reserves to 40 billion barrels, under its "Vision 2010" programme.
Nigeria currently pumps two million bpd with reserves of 20 billion barrels, which under a previous plan were to be raised by the year 2000 to 2.5 million bpd and 25 billion barrels, respectively.
Crude oil export contribute to well over 90 percent of Nigeria's total foreign exchange income.
